title: Adequate moduli spaces are universally submersive
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $f:\mathcal X\to Y$ an adequate moduli space [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space]. For every morphism $T\to Y$ of algebraic spaces over $k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], the induced continuous map $|\mathcal X\times_YT|\to|T|$ is surjective, and a subset $V\subseteq|T|$ is open if and only if its inverse image is open. Here the underlying space of an algebraic stack consists of field-valued objects up to isomorphism after common field extension, with the quotient topology from a smooth surjective scheme atlas; the topology on an algebraic space is defined by any surjective etale scheme atlas. There is no Noetherian, finite-type or separatedness hypothesis on $Y$.

source.place: Alper arXiv:1005.2398v3, Theorem 5.3.1 (1)--(3), including arbitrary algebraic-space base change; its proof uses Proposition 5.2.9 (3). Read online https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary morphism $g:T\to Y$ of algebraic spaces over $k$, and put $h:|\mathcal X\times_YT|\to|T|$. By [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-topological-images], $|f|$ is surjective. The image-base-change assertion of [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets], applied to $\mathcal X\to Y\leftarrow T$ (regarding spaces as stacks with discrete groupoids), gives $\operatorname{im}h=|g|^{-1}(\operatorname{im}|f|)=|T|$. Thus $h$ is surjective. The same topology node supplies continuity of $h$ and the agreement with the atlas topologies used in the statement.

For this same arbitrary algebraic-space base change $T\to Y$, [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-topological-images] states that $h$ sends every closed subset to a closed subset. Apply that assertion directly to the original adequate moduli space $f$. No assertion that $\mathcal X\times_YT\to T$ is itself adequate is needed, and no flatness hypothesis is imposed on $g$.

source.place: Alper arXiv:1005.2398v3, Theorem 5.3.1(1)--(3), especially the last implication (1),(2) imply (3); read https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3, local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Let $V\subseteq|T|$. If $V$ is open, continuity of $h$ gives openness of $h^{-1}(V)$. Conversely suppose $h^{-1}(V)$ is open. Its complement $C=h^{-1}(|T|\setminus V)$ is closed, so Step 2 makes $h(C)$ closed. Surjectivity from Step 1 gives $h(C)=|T|\setminus V$: every point outside $V$ has a preimage, and every point of $C$ maps outside $V$. Hence $V$ is open. Since $g$ was arbitrary, this proves every assertion of the item.
